**Epic red-line review of #32001 (G1 #31691 part c, `/automation`) at head 543640e9: PASS.** It lands once CI is green and the seat's contract review is done.

- **One rule, no second identity.** An addressed flow or connector path is served exactly as its bare path, and only when the engine's own resolver (`resolvePackageScopedName`) answers the bare name with the package the namespace names. The engine arms one flow per bare name, so the address asserts which flow is meant. It never picks one.
  - When nothing holds the name in that namespace, the answer is 404 naming the namespace.
  - When another package holds it, the answer is 409 naming the holders.
  - When co-owners both hold it, the answer is 409 naming both.
  - `_env` serves only an environment item. P's package-less overlay belongs to P (D4), so `_env` for it answers 409 naming P. That is correct.
- **Gates first.** The gates judge the bare shape before the address is weighed, so an addressed path can never reach past a gate its bare path meets.
- **Narrowings are declared with a first-party count of 0.**
  - A by-name read of a bare name two packages hold now answers 409. The engine already refuses to arm such a name, so before this the answer was a misleading 404, or the connection door passed the name through unqualified.
  - The legacy `trigger/:x/:y` is declined. On a catch-all host it used to run `:x` and ignore `:y`, which is the same loose-parse class as #31979.
  - The unserved 2- and 3-segment shapes are declined.
  - The domain answers the 405s with `Allow`.
- **Owed pin is delivered.** The qualified `/meta/:type/:ns/:name` pin for agent and skill, owed by G1 since #31973 landed first, is here in the dogfood test (`alpha`/`beta` each serve their own item).

**Before G1 #31691 closes:** this PR leaves out the qualified inbound hook (`/automation/hooks/:flowName/:hookId`). Either the PR that carries `Fixes #31691` covers it, or the card names where it goes, for example B #31696 (flow) or B #31699 (webhook). B #31696, #31697, #31699 and #31700 open when #31691 closes, so it must not close with that address unassigned.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `543640e930bdc4416d1eb71b69ccc0af6025fb95`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-address.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-addressed-route.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/automation-every-verb.hono.integration.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.conformance.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.anonymous-gate.integration.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.automation-clone-mount.integration.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.dogfood.test.ts + packages/spec/src/kernel/address-grammar.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md (D3, D4, D5, the G1 and E1 rows), all read on `main` at c9246279a, never reviewed

Inputs: card #31691 (body and all 6 comments), PR #32001 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), the check-runs on the head. Read-only: nothing built or run.

Check-runs on the head when this record was written: 15 succeeded, none failed, 19 still in progress, so those gate verdicts are not in yet: Build Core; Test Core 1/8 to 8/8; Type Check · workspace; Type Check · consumer gates; Lint · CI, release & engine gates; Lint · PM dispatch-gates; Lint · docs & code guards; Lint · repo & tooling gates; Lint · scoped · query-options erasure; Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus; Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests; Live E2E UI. Succeeded: Check Changeset (2), Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Check PR Size, Plan Test Core shards, Test UI, docs flag, filter, Auto Label. The route-ledger pins, the envelope gate and both new test files run in the jobs still in progress. The verdict below does not depend on them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Sixteen addressed routes are new surface (16 `server-only` ledger rows, census 131 to 147, 16 mounts per base). Right: each was no route on `main`, and the mounts are registered after every bare mount.
2. A bare by-name door whose name two packages hold answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with candidates (`bareByNameRefusal`). Right in principle: it is D5's own bare-address answer, and `main`'s engine already refuses to arm such a name (`engine.ts` 4639 to 4644). Wrong at one edge: finding S1.
3. An addressed path is served only when the bare name resolves, for a caller with no package, to the addressed holder (`admitAutomationAddress`). Right as an honest refusal over an engine that arms one flow per bare name. Its consequence is that the address of a two-holder name answers the same `409`, which the PR's own test pins. The declaration says the opposite: finding M1.
4. `trigger/:x/:y` with no address is declined. Right for `POST`, and needed (otherwise `trigger/crm/foo` with `crm` not installed would run the flow `crm`). Wrong for the other verbs: finding S2.
5. The domain answers `405` with `Allow` from `automationRouteAllow` for a served shape under another verb. Right on the mounted host, where only two-segment paths newly reach the domain. On the catch-all host the same `405` replaces `404` at every served depth (one, three and four segments too; the PR's test pins the one-segment case), which the declaration states for two segments only: part of M1.
6. Every two- and three-segment path now reaches the domain, so anonymous callers get `401` and unserved shapes get `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. Right: the domain's floor is its first statement and reads the raw path.
7. The gates read the stripped shape, and the stripped shape is exactly the bare path that is then served, so no addressed path is served behind a narrower gate than its bare path. Right, and I could not break it: every stripped path is a bare path the same caller could send. One nit under ④.
8. `check-route-envelope.mjs`: `automation.ts` declares one hand-built `405` (it carries `Allow`, body through `buildApiError`). Right, and it matches the diff: one hand-built response.
9. Forced test edits (the #19543 control moved to a four-segment path, the clone mount's negative control moved one segment deeper). Right: both follow from judgment 6, and neither loosens what the test proves.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime: patch` is the right level: nothing a metadata author writes changes (`Metadata-protocol: none` is right), and AGENTS.md rule 3 ships a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, as `patch` with its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 marker. Both are present, and `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right for stored metadata.

Clause-②: no (narrowing). Right arm, present line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. The body of the declaration is not right: see M1. The rule's own text asks a breaking changeset for its FROM to TO mapping and one-line fix, and one of the two mappings given does not work at this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags and open questions:
- Names (`automation-address.ts`, `readAutomationAddress`, `admitAutomationAddress`, `automationRouteAllow`, `AUTOMATION_FLOW_SUBRESOURCE_SEGMENTS`), no new error code: accepted. D5 forbids a new code and none is minted.
- The legacy trigger past three segments stays unbounded: accepted as left, with the follow-up card. It is base behaviour, and no addressed shape is that deep. The card should also carry `POST trigger/runs/:runId/resume` running the flow `runs`.
- SDK rows `server-only`: accepted.

Escalated to the seat (none of these is mine to settle):
- E1. The PR, the module note and the code comments cite "seat ruling Q1 = A", "Q2" and "Q3 = A" on #31691 for part (c). None of them is on the card: its six comments hold triage, two carrier notes, the claim, part (a)'s report and the B note. The rulings need to be on the card before a record can rest on them. I judged the three choices on the tree instead: Q1 (a sub-resource literal in the name position keeps the bare route) keeps more bare behaviour than D5's step 2 does and is the rule part (a) merged with; Q3 (strip before the gates) holds, judgment 7; Q2 (serve only what the bare name resolves to) holds as a refusal, with M1.
- E2. The card's `Narrowing:` line lists the `/actions` arity narrowing, added and ruled at part (b). It lists none of this PR's narrowings 2, 3 and 4 (the trigger arity, the `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND` to `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` and `401` answers, the domain's `405`). The card's acceptance says a narrowing beyond the declared one goes to the maintainer before landing. The epic seat rules them as it did at part (b), on the card, or escalates.
- E3. ADR-0150 on `main` still declares that a package-qualified address reaches the intended holder of a two-holder name (line 293) and that the engine keys flows by `(package, name)` with all same-named flows arming (the D4 table). `main`'s engine arms one flow per bare name and cites #31677 Q1 for it. That is a capability declared and not delivered: it is implemented or retired by an ADR amendment card, and this PR does neither. It needs a card.
- E4. The B note (6750690282) owes one pin: each qualified address serves its own agent and skill, `_env` serves only an environment item, the bare read stays 409, on both transports. The added dogfood test pins the two qualified reads on one transport. The `_env` leg and the second transport are not pinned here. Either they are added, or the card says which later part carries them.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against D5 on `main`. The bare `409` makes the spec's own refusal real: D5 says a bare address with more than one holder answers `409` with candidates, and before this PR the doors answered `404` or the engine's error for a name the engine had already refused to arm. Nothing that was served is taken away, with the exceptions below. The admission rule does not narrow a delivered capability either: the engine holds no flow under a two-holder name, so the door has nothing to serve and refuses, naming both. That part of the design holds.

**M1, must-fix (prose faces: the changeset and the PR body).** The declaration prescribes "FROM a bare name two packages hold TO its addressed path". At this head the addressed path of a two-holder name answers the same `409`: `admitAutomationAddress` returns the bare resolution's refusal (`if (bare.status === 'refused')`), and `automation-addressed-route.test.ts` pins it ("a bare name two packages hold: its address is refused naming both"). So the BREAKING notice that ships in `CHANGELOG.md` tells a reader to move to a path this release refuses. The honest statement is that a two-holder flow or connector name has no served door until one holder is renamed or removed (or the engine is keyed by package, E3). The same edit should state narrowing 4 for what the tree does: on the catch-all host `404` becomes `405` on every served shape, not only two-segment ones. The fix is on the prose faces alone and moves no code.

**S1, should-fix.** `bareByNameItem` reads every one-segment `GET` as a flow read, the domain's own literals included. With two packages each holding a flow named `actions` (or `_status`, for a row saved before child P's refusal), `GET /automation/actions`, the action catalog, answers `409` instead of the catalog, because the refusal runs before the catalog arm. The catalog names no flow. This is a narrowing nobody declared, on a route first-party clients call. Fix: `bareByNameItem` returns nothing for the door's literal segments.

**S2, should-fix.** `if (parts[0] === 'trigger' && parts.length === 3) return { handled: false };` declines every verb, where the arm it guards is `POST` only. `GET /automation/trigger/runs/:runId`, the run read of a flow named `trigger`, was served on `main` by the `/:name/runs/:runId` arm and is now `404`, while the two-segment and four-segment doors of the same flow still answer. The declared narrowing is `POST` only. Fix: scope the decline to `POST`.

**S3, should-fix.** After a qualifier, the name position is not checked against the door's literals, and the stripped path is handed to the literal arms. `readAutomationAddress` turns `/automation/_env/actions` into `['actions']` with the item "flow `actions`"; `_env` admits it when no package holds that name; the catalog arm then answers. The same holds for `_status` and `connectors`, and on a catch-all host `POST /automation/_env/trigger/foo` is admitted against a flow named `trigger` and then runs the flow `foo` through the legacy arm, whether or not the environment holds `foo`. That contradicts the declared rule that `_env` serves only the environment's own item, and the module note's "after `_env` the segment is always the name". No gate is passed by it (the stripped path is a bare path behind its own gates, and the engine's own refusal still stops a two-holder name), so it is an alias with a wrong admission, not an escalation. Fix: a qualifier followed by one of the door's literals is declined, or routed only to the flow arms.

**N1, nit.** The address is read before the capability gates, so an authenticated caller without the capability can tell an installed namespace from none: `POST /automation/crm/x/toggle` answers `403` when `crm` is installed and `404` when it is not. The comment "a refused caller learns nothing about it" is true of the holder, not of the namespace. Namespaces are not secret elsewhere; left as an accepted deviation, or the comment is corrected.

A must-fix stands, so this round fails. M1 is fixed on the prose faces; S1, S2 and S3 move the head and earn a delta review.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **M1 is closed.** The changeset and the body now say that the qualified address of a name two packages hold answers the same 409, and they give the real migration: rename or delete one package's flow (or instance). Narrowing 4 is stated as the tree does it: on a mounted host only two-segment paths change, and on a catch-all host every served depth from one to four segments goes from 404 to 405. Right.

4. **S3 is closed.** `AUTOMATION_DOOR_LITERALS` reads `NAMESPACE_POSITION_LITERALS.automation.literals` (`_status`, `actions`, `connectors`, `hooks`, `trigger`) from the one place they live. After a qualifier, a door literal in the name position reads as `declined`, and the domain answers it as an unserved shape before anything runs. After a namespace, Q1's sub-resource rule is asked first, so `crm/runs` keeps its bare route. 6. **E4 is closed.** B's dogfood file adds the `_env` leg (409 naming both holders) and a second transport (the runtime dispatcher's `/meta` on the same booted kernel). It pins alpha, beta, `_env` and the bare read on both.
